Deepen Fundamental Research in Plastic Pyrolysis Mechanisms and Predictive Modeling Despite progress, the fundamental chemistry of plastic pyrolysis remains poorly understood, particularly for mixed and contaminated waste streams. Accurate prediction of product distributions is essential for reactor design and process optimization. Future R&D needs include expanding mechanistic reaction networks, integrating quantum- chemical data, and validating models at pilot scale. Commercialization opportunities include licensing kinetic models and simulation tools. Remaining technical risks include incomplete mechanistic understanding and limited pilot-scale validation. 5. Launch a National Public Education and Technical Communication Initiative Public misunderstanding of recycling technologies remains a major barrier to achieving high- quality feedstocks and widespread adoption of chemical recycling. DOE should lead the creation of a national, science-based public education initiative. Future needs include development of a public information platform, K–12 curriculum, and partnerships with municipalities and NGOs. Barriers include misinformation, inconsistent messaging, and lack of public trust. Opportunities include adoption of educational materials by schools and local governments. 6. Future Research and Development Plans, Technology Transfer, and Commercialization Pathways CUWP would like to continue work in all five areas described above. However, we currently have no funding to pursue this work, except for limited DOE grants related to STRAP. Without sustained DOE support, the scientific and engineering momentum built through CUWP will be lost. Appropriate next R&D steps include: (1) advancing sorting technologies and feedstock standards; (2) operating and scaling the STRAP pilot plant; (3) scaling surfactant production and expanding application testing; (4) deepening mechanistic understanding of pyrolysis; and (5) launching a national public education initiative. Technology transfer opportunities include licensing of STRAP and hydroformylation to surfactant patents, deployment of advanced sorting systems, and commercialization of plastic-derived surfactants. Remaining technical risks include feedstock variability, solvent degradation, catalyst stability, and lack of pilot-scale validation. Barriers to commercialization include capital costs, regulatory uncertainty, and limited public awareness. 6.
